newsitem.title: INDIA: India telecom regulations are risky - Dun & Phelps.
newsitem.headline: India telecom regulations are risky - Dun & Phelps.

text.p: Regulatory risk is the single largest risk hindering India's telecommunications industry, Dun & Phelps Credit Rating India Private Ltd said on Friday.
The agency said the newly set-up independent Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) was likely to take some time to become fully operational.

"Until that time, the department of telecommunications (DoT) would continue to play the dual role of an operator and a regulator and the industry would be vulnerable to adverse changes in regulations," the credit rating firm said in a report on the sector.
"Tariff barriers imposed by DoT also deter the telecom operators from flexibility," it said, pointing out that tariffs charged by private operators could not exceed those of DoT.
India's low call completion rates along with a fixed line penetration of just 1.3 telephones per 100 people were the positive factors, Dun & Phelps said.
India began opening its telecommunications sector as part of its gradual conversion to a free-market economy from 1991.
Dun & Phelps said high investment levels, mostly due to licence fees and infrastructure costs, would be an effective entry barrier for new players.

The license fees to be paid by operators amount to 44 percent of the total investment in the first five years, while the total license fee required for cellular service operators over a 10 year period is 200.8 billion rupees, Dun & Phelps said.
"Existing licensees would need to seek finance from international markets in order to meet the fund requirements," the credit rating agency said.
It said the domestic debt envisaged by fixed line and cellular operators over the next five years would total around 72.50 billion rupees.
"With the recent relaxation in external commercial borrowings guidelines, telecom projects would be able to fund 50 percent of their project cost through ECBs."
